content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has not received recommendations from China regarding certain treatments. In general hospitals, 4% (1037 out of 1580) of cases were reported. Nine factors were significantly associated with non-adherence to treatment guidelines. These include working in northern China, being employed in general hospitals, working in the urology department, diagnosing more cases (11–30 cases) in the past six months, and lacking knowledge of the regimens for treating gonorrhea as outlined in the National STD Guidelines. Only 1% of health facilities had intramuscular ceftriaxone available in stock. A study conducted by Wynn in 2016 demonstrated the feasibility of implementing sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing interventions for pregnant women in a hospital antenatal clinic in Botswana. Among 225 eligible women who were offered participation, 200 (89%) accepted. The primary reasons for non-acceptance included lack of time (40%, n=10) and unwillingness to undergo additional testing (8%, n=2). Two women (8%) did not provide a reason, while four (16%) stated they would return later for testing but ultimately did not. The WHO guidelines for the treatment of Neisseria gonorrhoeae include systematic reviews and evidence-based recommendations. Studies have explored various treatment regimens, including ceftriaxone, azithromycin, and alternative therapies, to address antimicrobial resistance and optimize treatment outcomes. Research has also investigated the persistence of gonococcal DNA following treatment, influenced by antibiotic susceptibility and reinfection rates. Randomized controlled trials have compared the efficacy of different antibiotics, such as solithromycin versus ceftriaxone plus azithromycin, ertapenem, gentamicin, fosfomycin, and other regimens for treating uncomplicated gonorrhea. Studies have also evaluated single-dose therapies, including oral delafloxacin, zoliflodacin, and ceftriaxone, for their safety and effectiveness in treating urogenital and pharyngeal infections caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Further research has examined the cost-effectiveness of targeted therapies, such as gyrase A testing and ciprofloxacin therapy, compared to dual-drug regimens. Investigations into antibiotic resistance patterns and treatment failures have highlighted the need for updated guidelines and alternative treatment options, particularly in regions with high resistance rates. Overall, the body of evidence underscores the importance of adherence to treatment guidelines, the availability of effective antibiotics, and the implementation of diagnostic-based treatment strategies to combat gonorrhea and other sexually transmitted infections.
